eda_round_question: Given that per-candidate valid-split deltas are largely within the metric's own sampling noise, the more promising path is probably a genuinely new signal source (not another small reweighting/regularization/capacity tweak to the same 5-field FM) — but I don't know what's actually available in the raw data beyond what's already been tried (user/video side fields, historical rates, tab, duration). I'd like a fresh exploratory EDA pass to look for anything with a plausibly LARGE effect size (e.g. strong temporal/session structure, video content/category signal, or user-activity-level segmentation where the FM might be systematically failing) that could produce a gap big enough to clear the ~0.005-0.006 noise floor, rather than continuing to guess at marginal single-digit-per-mille tweaks.
reflection: The probe confirmed the plateau's root cause: the valid-split primary metric has a bootstrap p5-p95 range of ~0.0055 and std of ~0.0017 under a completely fixed scoring function, which is comparable to or larger than nearly every gap (0.002-0.007) that has separated accepted from rejected candidates over the last 7 iterations. This means most of those "rejections" may simply be noise, not evidence the mechanisms don't work — so continuing to propose small variants of the same FM-capacity/regularization/reweighting mechanisms and reading their single-run valid deltas as ground truth is no longer a reliable strategy.
